AMENDED JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed under the provisions of Sec.166 of M.V Act,
1988 seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the death of Manjunath S/o. Ramalingaiah caused in a Road Traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under:
It is the case of the petitioners that on 26.06.2020 at about 1.40 a.m., the deceased Manjunath was travelling from Bangalore to Dharmastala along with his friends in Tata Etios Car bearing reg.No.KA03AE4295.

When they reached near Karthikere village, the driver of the car lost his control in a curving road and dashed against the left side signal light pole as a result, the car toppled for 45 times and due to impact the deceased died at the spot.

Further it is the case of the petitioners that with respect to accident, FIR came to be registered in Crime No.159/2020 at Chikkamangaluru Rural Circle police station against the driver of the Tata Etios Car bearing reg.No.KA03AE4295 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC r/w Section 187 of IMV Act.

3. Further it is the case of the petitioners that deceased Manjunath was Barber by occupation and maintaining Saloon in the name Manju Gent's Parlour by employing 34 members and earning Rs.60,000/ per month.
He was only the earning member SCCH - 26 4 MVC No.2981/2020 in the family.
Further they have stated that due to untimely death of deceased, they lost their beloved son.
They have also stated that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

They have further stated that Respondent No.1 being the owner,
Respondent No.2 being the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, they have prayed to award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ from the Respondents.

Ramalingaiah vs Mr. Naveen Kumar on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89734429/
2 4.
The notice of the petition has been duly served on Respondent No.1 and 2.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before this tribunal and filed their respective written statement.
The respondent No.1 has denied the entire case of the petitioners as false and baseless.

However, he has admitted that FIR in crime No.159/2020 has been registered against the driver of Tata Etios Car bearing reg.No.KA03AE 4295 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337, 304 A of IPC r/w.Section 187 of IMV Act.
Hence, he has prayed to reject the petition against him.
The Respondent No.2 has denied the entire case of the petitioners as false and baseless.
He has further denied the issuance of policy bearing No.P0020400002/4104/104165 in favour of Respondent No.1 with respect to car bearing No. KA 03AE4295.
Further he has contended that the owner of the vehicle or the police have not complied with the provisions of IMV Act after the accident.
He has also contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
He has also contended that the Respondent No.1 willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

As such, Respondent No.1 has committed breach of condition policy as such,
he is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. Initially, this case has been clubbed with MVC No.2980/2020 as the cause of action is same arising out of same accident.
But on 23.11.2022 the Petitioners in MVC SCCH - 26 6 MVC No.2981/2020 No.2980/2020 have entered into compromise with Respondent No.2 for sum of Rs.25,00,000/ and filed joint memo in this regard.
However, in the present petition the parties have not entered into compromise.
Hence, the present petition has been separated from MVC No.2980/2020.

7. On the basis of the above pleadings my predecessor in office has framed the following issues :
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioners proves

that, deceased Manjunath S/o Ramalingaiah, was dies in a road traffic accident that occurred on 27062020 at about 01.40 a.m.
deceased was travelling in his friend's car Tata Etios Car bearing No.KA03AE 4295, when they reached Belur Chikkamangaluru road, just 5 kms away from Chikkamangaluru, near Karthikeri village, taluk and Chikkamangaluru district, at that time the driver of the said car drove in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the left side signal light pole and car tilted.
As a result deceased sustained fatal injuries and died, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition?

If so,
from which Respondent?

3. What Order or Award?
8.
The Petitioner No.2 has got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 11 documents as Ex's.P1 to 9 and as Ex.P.15 and 16.
Respondents have not led any evidence on their behalf.
9. Heard the arguments from both sides.
Perused the entire records.

10. My answers to the above issues are as follows : Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 11. ISSUE NO.1:

It is the case of the petitioners that on 26.06.2020 at about 1.40 a.m., the deceased Manjunath was travelling from Bangalore to Dharmastala along with his friends in Tata Etios Car bearing reg.No.KA03AE4295.

When they reached near Karthikere village, the driver of the car lost his SCCH - 26 8 MVC No.2981/2020 control in a curving road and dashed against the left side signal light pole as a result, the car toppled for 45 times and due to impact the deceased died at the spot.

In this regard, FIR came to be registered in Crime No.159/2020 at Chikkamangaluru Rural Circle police station against the driver of the Tata Etios Car bearing reg.No.KA03AE4295 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC r/w Section 187 of IMV Act.
12.
As already stated supra, petitioner No.2 has examined herself as PW1 and got marked 11 documents as ExP.1 to P.9 and Ex.P.15 and 16.
She has filed affidavit in lieu of her examinationinchief reiterating entire petition averments.

13. From the evidence on record it can be seen that after receipt of complaint lodged by one Mohan S S/o. Suresh, the Chikkamagaluru Rural police have registered FIR in Crime No.169/2020 against the driver of Tata Etios Car bearing No.KA03AE 4295 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 304A of IPC.
After due investigation the police have filed chargesheet SCCH - 26 9 MVC No.2981/2020 against the driver of the vehicle for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 338, 304(A) of IPC.
Though the learned counsel for the Respondent No.2 has cross examined PW1 but he has failed to elicit anything from her to disbelieve her version.

14. On the other hand though the Respondents have denied the entire case of the Petitioners but they have not adduced any evidence to over come the evidence of the petitioners with respect to date, time and place of accident and with respect to death of deceased in the said accident.

Ramalingaiah vs Mr. Naveen Kumar on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89734429/
4
Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
As per the charge sheet the accident occurred due to rash and negligent of driver of Tata Etios Car bearing No.KA03AE4295.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compared to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the chapter in M.V.Act dealing with SCCH - 26 10 MVC No.2981/2020 compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, based on the above discussion, I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the Tata Etios Car bearing reg.No.KA03AE4295 is proved.
As such, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2: LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:
PW.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhar cards at ExP8 and 9 and Ration card at Ex.P.15.
As per these documents, petitioner No.1 is the father and petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased.
It is relevant to note that petitioner No.1, the father of the deceased, is aged about 57 years and petitioner No.2, the mother of the deceased, is aged about 45 years.
As such they considered as dependents on the deceased.
Hence, petitioner No.1 and 2 are entitled for compensation under the head loss of dependency.
16. As per ExP8 - Aadhar card of deceased, the date of birth of deceased shown as 01.01.1995.
It indicates that he was SCCH - 26 11 MVC No.2981/2020 aged about 25 years as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the appropriate multiplier as per Sarala Verma's Case for the said age group is "18".
17.

PW1 has stated in her affidavit that prior to the accident the deceased was very hale and healthy and was running Gent's Parlour and earning Rs.60,000/ p.m. and contributing the same towards the family maintenance.
But PW.1 has not produced any document to prove the avocation and income of the deceased.
Hence, in the absence of proof of avocation and income, this tribunal has to consider notional income for calculating the compensation.

As per the guidelines issued by Karnataka State Legal Service Authority the notional income of the deceased is taken as Rs.14,500/
as the accident took place in the year 2020.
18. In the present case the deceased was aged about 25 years.
His notional income is taken as Rs.14,500/ p.m.

In decision reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court cases 680 SCCH - 26 12 MVC No.2981/2020 (National Insurance company Ltd., Vs Pranay Sethi and others), 40% income is to be added towards future prospectus.

Therefore, the total income comes to Rs.20,300/ (Rs.14,500/+ Rs.5,800/).
The deceased was bachelor and there is only two dependents.
Hence,  is to be deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased.

Income for consideration is Rs.10,150/
(Rs.20,300/  Rs.10,150/).
Annual income worksout to Rs.10,150/ x 12 = Rs.1,21,800/.
Appropriate multiplier is "18".

Thus loss of dependency worksout to Rs.1,21,800/ x 18 =
Rs.21,92,400/.
19. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in civil Appeal No.2705/2020 in the case of United India Insurance company Ltd., Vs Satinder Kaur and others, each of the claimants are entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/ each on account of loss of Ramalingaiah vs Mr. Naveen Kumar on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89734429/
5 consortium and loss of love and affection.
SCCH - 26 13 MVC No.2981/2020 20.

sentences.text: LOSS OF ESTATE:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards loss of estate.
21. FUNERAL EXPENSES:
Petitioners are entitled for Rs.15,000/ towards funeral expenses.

22. The calculation table stands as follows : 1 Loss of dependency Rs. 21,92,400=00 (Petitioner No.1 and 2) 2 Loss of consortium to Rs. 80,000=00 (Rs.40,000/ each) 3 Loss of estate Rs.
15,000=00 4 Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000=00

GRAND TOTAL Rs. 23,02,400=00 Hence, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.23,02,400/.
23.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner of offending Tata Etios Car bearing reg.No.KA03AE4295.
The Respondent No.2 at para No.3 of his written statement has denied the issuance of policy in favour of Respondent No.1 with respect to car bearing No.KA03AE 4295.

But at para No.6 of his written statement he has contended that the Respondent No.1 willfully entrusted the said car to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident as such, he breached the terms and conditions of the policy.
Therefore, it clearly indicates that Respondent No.2 at one hand disputes the issuance of policy but on the other hand he admits the breach of policy.
Ex.P.7
the certified copy of chargesheet consists of copy of insurance policy.
From this document it is clear that the Respondent No.2 has issued policy with respect to offending car bearing reg.No.KA 03AE4295 which was valid from 29.07.2019 to 28.07.2020.
Therefore, it is clear that the policy issued by the Respondent No.2 was valid as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the Respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle and Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award SCCH - 26 15 MVC No.2981/2020 amount to the petitioners together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
The primary liability is on the Respondent No.2 to pay the above said compensation amount with interest.

Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the affirmative'.

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
: ORDER : The petition filed Under Section 166 of M.V Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :

from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation SCCH - 26 16 MVC No.2981/2020 amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1  25%

 Out of the share amount of petitioner No.1 and 2, a sum equal to 75% each shall be released in their favour through Epayment on proper identification and verification and the remaining 25%

The Petitioner No.1 and 2 are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on their deposit amount from time to time.

Draw an award accordingly.
